documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER, BIRTHING UNIT
Admit 11/7/2025 21:30. Discharge 11/9/2025.

27 y/o G1P0 at 39w4d admitted in spontaneous active labor. Pregnancy notable for hyperemesis gravidarum in the first trimester with two ED visits, resolved by 20 weeks. Otherwise uncomplicated prenatal course. NKDA.

Delivery 11/8/2025 04:52 at 39w5d: spontaneous vaginal delivery of a liveborn infant, vigorous at birth, routine newborn care. Placenta delivered intact. Estimated blood loss within normal range. No laceration requiring repair.

Postpartum course uncomplicated. Ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet, pain controlled. Vital signs normal throughout.

Discharge diagnosis: term spontaneous vaginal delivery.
Meds at discharge: prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Follow-up: obstetrics postpartum visit in about 6 weeks.

documents.title: Delivery discharge summary received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Discharge summary from birthing unit, 11/7-11/9/2025, received via fax and scanned. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Congratulations
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Leah, I just saw the hospital summary come through. Congratulations to you all. Rest up, and reach out if you need anything. Your OB will see you in about six weeks; after that, let's get you in here sometime this winter.

documents.title: Obstetrics postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRIC GROUP
Postpartum visit, 12/17/2025

Six weeks after a spontaneous vaginal delivery at 39w5d. Recovering well. Bleeding stopped. Mood good, sleeping in stretches. Pelvic exam normal, uterus involuted. BP normal.
Continue prenatal vitamin while recovering. Return to us as needed; routine primary care with her PCP.

--- Filed.

documents.title: Prenatal vitamin refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request, prenatal vitamin with iron daily #90. Last seen 9/5/25. Approved x1 per protocol; note to pt that she is due for a visit.

documents.title: News
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to let you know I'm pregnant again! Earlier than we planned, but we're happy. LMP was February 2. I already saw my OB group and the early ultrasound looked good. So far no vomiting at all, fingers crossed. Still taking the prenatal vitamin. I know I owe you a visit, the baby has made it hard to get anywhere. Anything I should be doing?

documents.title: RE: News
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, Leah. That puts you around 5 weeks, due early November. Keep the prenatal vitamin. Since you had hyperemesis last time, don't be a hero if it starts again: tell your OB early, the medicines work better before you're dehydrated. Come see me when life allows; no rush on our end.

reports.text: Indication: right flank pain, pregnant, 9 weeks. Right kidney 11.2 cm, normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. Mild right hydronephrosis. A 5 mm echogenic shadowing stone at the right ureterovesical junction with twinkle artifact. Right ureteral jet not seen during the exam; left jet present. Left kidney 11.0 cm, normal, no hydronephrosis or stone. Bladder normal. Limited view of the uterus shows an intrauterine pregnancy with fetal cardiac activity.
reports.conclusion: 5 mm right ureterovesical junction stone with mild right hydronephrosis. Normal left kidney. Intrauterine pregnancy with cardiac activity.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
COMMUNITY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT

CC: right flank pain.

27 y/o G2P1 at 9w6d (LMP 2/2/26). Sudden severe right flank pain starting around 8 PM, now 6 hours, moving down into the right groin. Nauseated, has not vomited. No fever, no burning, no frequency. Prenatal course so far has been uncomplicated, no hyperemesis this time. Last here a year ago with hyperemesis in her first pregnancy.

PMH: hyperemesis gravidarum (prior pregnancy). PSH: tonsillectomy, wisdom teeth. Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA.
Family: maternal uncle with recurrent calcium oxalate stones; mother hyperemesis; paternal grandmother DM2.
Never smoker, no alcohol (pregnant), teacher.

Vitals: afebrile, BP 125/78, HR 88.
Exam: uncomfortable, shifting on the stretcher. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, no peritoneal signs. No vaginal bleeding.

UA: microscopic hematuria, nitrite and LE negative, rare WBC; no sign of infection. Culture sent.
CBC, BMP unremarkable, Cr 0.6.
Renal US (no CT in pregnancy): 5 mm right UVJ stone, mild right hydronephrosis, left kidney normal. Bedside view: IUP with cardiac activity.

Treatment: acetaminophen 1 g PO, 1 L LR. Pain from 9/10 to 3/10.

Impression: right ureterolithiasis, 5 mm distal stone, uncomplicated, in a 10-week pregnancy.
Plan: home. Acetaminophen 500 mg, 2 tabs every 6 hours as needed. Oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325, 1 tab every 6 h if pain is not controlled, #8, no refills. Strain urine, save the stone. Push fluids. Outpatient urology referral placed. OB notified. Return for fever, uncontrolled pain or vomiting, or bleeding.

documents.title: ED record 4/12/2026
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED note from 4/12 received: right 5 mm UVJ stone at ~10 weeks pregnant, sent home with acetaminophen and a few oxycodone tabs, urology referral from the ED. Scanned, routed to PCP. Pt not seen here since 9/2025.

documents.title: Checking in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Leah, we got your ER record from the weekend. How is the pain today? Let us know if you need help getting in with urology or if anything gets worse.

documents.title: RE: Checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. Comes and goes, mostly a dull ache now. Urology called me already, I see them May 6.

documents.title: Stone
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good news, I think I passed it last night! Caught it in the strainer. No pain at all this morning. Should I still go to urology?

documents.title: RE: Stone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. Yes, keep the urology visit and bring the stone with you. They'll want a quick ultrasound to make sure the kidney has drained, and they can talk about prevention given your uncle's history.

reports.text: Comparison 4/12/2026. Right kidney 11.1 cm and left kidney 11.0 cm with normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. No hydronephrosis on either side. No renal or ureterovesical junction stones seen. Bilateral ureteral jets present. Bladder normal.
reports.conclusion: Normal kidneys. Interval resolution of right hydronephrosis; no stones.

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY GROUP
Consultation, 5/6/2026
Referred from: emergency department. Copy to PCP.

27 y/o currently about 13 weeks pregnant, seen in the ED 4/12 with a 5 mm right UVJ stone and mild hydronephrosis. Passed the stone 4/20 into a strainer and has been pain-free since. No fever, no urinary symptoms. First stone. Maternal uncle with recurrent calcium oxalate stones.
Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: well, no CVA tenderness.
Renal ultrasound today: no hydronephrosis, no residual stones.

Assessment: right distal ureteral stone, passed spontaneously; obstruction resolved.
Plan:
- Fluids 2.5 to 3 liters a day, enough that urine stays pale.
- No routine imaging in pregnancy unless symptoms return.
- With a family history of recurrent stones, a metabolic evaluation (24-hour urine) is reasonable once she is done with pregnancy and nursing; she can call us then.
- Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Urology letter received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Urology consult 5/6/2026 received and scanned: stone passed, ultrasound clear, 24-hr urine after pregnancy. Routed to PCP for review.

reports.text: Single live intrauterine gestation, cephalic at time of scan. Biometry consistent with 20 weeks 1 day, concordant with dating. Complete anatomy survey normal including brain, face, spine, heart with four chambers and outflow tracts, abdomen, kidneys, bladder and limbs. Anterior placenta, clear of the os. Normal amniotic fluid. Cervical length normal.

documents.title: Obstetrics 20-week visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRIC GROUP
Progress note 6/23/2026, G2P1 at 20w1d.

Doing well. No nausea or vomiting this pregnancy. No flank pain since passing the stone in April. BP normal. Fetal heart tones normal. Anatomy scan normal today.
Continue prenatal vitamin and good fluid intake. RTC 4 weeks.

--- Filed.

documents.title: Prenatal vitamin refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx request prenatal vitamin with iron #90. Not seen since 9/2025; PCP okayed a 90-day fill given pregnancy. Portal note sent asking her to schedule when she can.
